issue: Is a competency-to-stand-trial challenge that was not raised in the trial court procedurally defaulted when raised later in habeas proceedings?

sides.position: Competency-to-stand-trial arguments not preserved at trial are subject to procedural default in habeas proceedings.
cases: United States v. Basham, 789 F.3d 358 (4th Cir. 2015)
Yang v. United States, 114 F.4th 899 (7th Cir. 2024)
United States v. Cabrera-Rivas, 142 F.4th 199 (4th Cir. 2025)

quote: It also should not go unacknowledged that this case is situated amidst a deep and entrenched circuit split involving at least eight federal courts of appeals about the preservation of arguments related to competency to stand trial.
cite: United States v. Cristian Cabrera-Rivas, 142 F.4th 199 (4th Cir. 2025)
